mission: Find any normal production write/index/reindex path that bypasses M6 direct materialization

entrypoints_inspected.name: runner.run()
entrypoints_inspected.claim: Calls _process_unit (line 914) which contains the M6 direct materialization hook (_unit_processor.py:548-593); M6 World finalization at runner.py:1132-1206; legacy conversion (index_legacy_db_into_m6) only when FW_CONTEXT_M6_LEGACY_CONVERSION=1 (default 0)
code_evidence: runner.py:914 — status, syms, refs, timing, tu_headers_list = _process_unit(...)
_unit_processor.py:548-593 — M6 DIRECT MATERIALIZATION hook: calls materialize_unit_into_m6 when _m6_write_authority (FW_CONTEXT_M6_WRITE_AUTHORITY default '1') and world_ctx is not None
_unit_processor.py:601 — if not _legacy_compat_on(): return early WITHOUT writing to legacy index.db (M5 default: legacy compat OFF)

runner.py:1141-1206 — M6 World finalization: finalize_m6_world when _m6_write_authority (default on); index_legacy_db_into_m6 ONLY when _m6_legacy_conversion (FW_CONTEXT_M6_LEGACY_CONVERSION default '0')
runner.py:506-510 — conn = open_db(db_path) is INSIDE 'if _legacy_compat:' block; in normal mode (default) the legacy index.db is NEVER created/opened
entrypoints_inspected.verdict: PASS — M6 direct materialization is the normal production path

entrypoints_inspected.name: reindex_file / reindex_file_impl
entrypoints_inspected.claim: In pure-M6 mode (legacy index.db absent, the default), takes _reindex_m6_direct path -> materialize_unit_into_m6. The denominator ALSO claims the legacy-DB branch 'publishes to M6 via _unit_processor' — this sub-claim is FALSE.
code_evidence: maintenance.py:2250 — db_path, cfg, project_id, root = _resolve_context(project_root, skip_ready_check=True)
readiness.py:97-100,125 — _resolve_context returns db_path = cfg.index.db_dir / cfg.project.id / 'index.db' (the LEGACY index.db path)
maintenance.py:2262-2275 — if not db_path.exists() and _m6_write_auth (FW_CONTEXT_M6_WRITE_AUTHORITY default '1') and m6_db_path.exists(): return _reindex_m6_direct(file_path, root, m6_db_path)
maintenance.py:2180 — _reindex_m6_direct calls materialize_unit_into_m6(store=store, parsed=parsed, ...) -> M6 DIRECT materialization

maintenance.py:1441-1603 — _reindex_parse_and_store (the LEGACY-DB branch, taken when index.db EXISTS): calls store_symbols_for_unit (ops.py) + certify_and_publish_for_unit (certify.py:1081) DIRECTLY — NOT through _process_processor

grep of ops.py for _process_unit|materialize_unit_into_m6|certify_and_publish|_unit_processor -> NO MATCHES (store_symbols_for_unit does NOT route through _unit_processor and does NOT call materialize_unit_into_m6)
certify.py:1081-1200 — certify_and_publish_for_unit opens index-v2.db (v2 store) and publishes facts there; it does NOT call materialize_unit_into_m6 and does NOT touch index-m6.db
runner.py:506-510 — in normal mode (_legacy_compat_on() False, the default) runner.run() does NOT call open_db(db_path), so index.db is NEVER created
denominator_reasoning_errors: FALSE: denominator claims 'When legacy DB DOES exist (compat mode), the original path runs and the v2 certify hook still publishes to M6 via _unit_processor.' The legacy reindex branch (_reindex_parse_and_store) does NOT route through _unit_processor — it calls store_symbols_for_unit (ops.py) and certify_and_publish_for_unit (certify.py) directly. certify_and_publish_for_unit writes to index-v2.db only, NOT index-m6.db. So when index.db exists, reindex_file does NOT materialize to M6 at all.

REACHABILITY of the legacy branch: only when index.db exists on disk, which in shipped normal mode (default config) NEVER happens (runner.run skips open_db when _legacy_compat_on() is False). The legacy branch is reachable only via (a) explicit FW_CONTEXT_LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY_MODE=1 opt-in, or (b) a stale index.db left by an older pre-M5 fw-context version (upgrade scenario). Neither is 'shipped normal mode'.
entrypoints_inspected.verdict: PASS in shipped normal mode (index.db never created -> _reindex_m6_direct taken). CAVEAT: the legacy-DB reindex branch, IF reached via compat/upgrade, does NOT materialize to M6 — an undocumented gap distinct from index_legacy_db_into_m6.

entrypoints_inspected.name: CLI watch (auto-reindex)
entrypoints_inspected.claim: Denominator claims watch 'calls reindex_file_impl for each changed file' and 'inherits the M6-direct path via the reindex_file fix'. The FIRST claim is INACCURATE; the conclusion (M6 direct) is still correct.
code_evidence: cli/_watch.py:5 (docstring) — 'calls reindex_file_impl for each changed file' — but this is the MODULE DOCSTRING, not the actual daemon behavior

mcp/daemon.py:671-677 — _run_index_async spawns: asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(sys.executable, '-u', '-m', 'fw_context_mcp.cli', 'index', '--background', ...) — a FULL index subprocess, NOT reindex_file_impl
mcp/daemon.py:433 — _reindex_loop calls _run_index_async(project_root, db_dir, force_refs=force_refs)
cli/_index.py:830,982 — cmd_index imports and calls runner.run() — which has M6 direct materialization via _process_unit
Therefore the watch path reaches M6 direct materialization via runner.run() -> _process_unit (M6 hook), NOT via reindex_file_impl as the denominator asserts
denominator_reasoning_errors: INACCURATE: denominator claims the watch path 'inherits the M6-direct path via the reindex_file fix (maintenance.py:2072 _reindex_m6_direct)'. The watch daemon does NOT call reindex_file_impl at all — it spawns 'fw-context index --background' (daemon.py:672), which routes through cmd_index -> runner.run() -> _process_unit (M6 hook). The M6-direct conclusion is correct, but the stated mechanism (reindex_file_impl inheritance) is wrong.
entrypoints_inspected.verdict: PASS — reaches M6 direct materialization via runner.run() (not via reindex_file_impl as claimed)

bypasses_found.path: reindex_file_impl legacy-DB branch (_reindex_parse_and_store) when index.db exists
bypasses_found.reason: Requires index.db to exist on disk. In shipped normal mode (default config, fresh state) runner.run() never creates index.db (open_db is inside 'if _legacy_compat:' at runner.py:509-510, and _legacy_compat_on() is False by default). The legacy branch is only reachable via (a) explicit FW_CONTEXT_LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY_MODE=1 opt-in, or (b) a stale index.db from an older pre-M5 fw-context version. Neither is 'normal shipped mode'.
bypasses_found.impact: IF reached (compat/upgrade), reindex_file would update legacy index.db and index-v2.db but NOT index-m6.db — leaving M6 stale. This is an undocumented gap distinct from the explicitly-gated index_legacy_db_into_m6 conversion path. The denominator's claim that this branch 'publishes to M6 via _unit_processor' is FALSE.
bypasses_found.classification: compat island / upgrade edge case — not a normal-mode bypass

denominator_reasoning_errors: FALSE: reindex_file entry claims 'When legacy DB DOES exist (compat mode), the original path runs and the v2 certify hook still publishes to M6 via _unit_processor.' The legacy reindex branch (_reindex_parse_and_store, maintenance.py:1441) does NOT route through _unit_processor — it calls store_symbols_for_unit (ops.py) and certify_and_publish_for_unit (certify.py:1081) directly. certify_and_publish_for_unit writes to index-v2.db ONLY, never to index-m6.db. So the legacy-DB reindex branch does NOT publish to M6 at all.

INACCURATE: CLI watch entry claims the watch path 'inherits the M6-direct path via the reindex_file fix (maintenance.py:2072 _reindex_m6_direct)'. The watch daemon (mcp/daemon.py:671-677) does NOT call reindex_file_impl — it spawns 'fw-context index --background' as a subprocess, which routes through cmd_index -> runner.run() -> _process_unit (M6 hook). The M6-direct conclusion is correct but the stated mechanism is wrong.

MISLEADING: cli/_watch.py:5 docstring says the daemon 'calls reindex_file_impl for each changed file' — the actual daemon (mcp/daemon.py) spawns a full fw-context index --background subprocess per change burst, not reindex_file_impl per file.
reasoning: In shipped normal mode (default config, fresh state, no env overrides), NO normal production write/index/reindex path bypasses M6 direct materialization. (1) runner.run() materializes per-TU via _unit_processor.py:548-593 (materialize_unit_into_m6) and finalizes the M6 World at runner.py:1185 — the legacy index.db is never even opened (open_db is inside 'if _legacy_compat:' at runner.py:509-510, and _legacy_compat_on() is False by default). (2) reindex_file_impl checks 'if not db_path.exists()' at maintenance.py:2266; since index.db is never created in normal mode, it takes the _reindex_m6_direct branch -> materialize_unit_into_m6 (maintenance.py:2180). (3) The watch daemon spawns 'fw-context index --background' (daemon.py:672) -> runner.run() -> M6 direct. (4) index_legacy_db_into_m6 is gated behind FW_CONTEXT_M6_LEGACY_CONVERSION=1 (default 0). (5) reset_index is destructive, not materialization. (6) No other CLI/MCP path writes semantic state. The only code that does NOT materialize to M6 is the legacy-DB reindex branch (_reindex_parse_and_store), which is unreachable in normal mode because index.db is never created; it requires explicit compat opt-in or a stale DB from an older fw-context version — an upgrade/compat edge case, not 'normal shipped mode'. The denominator's CONCLUSION (normal_write_entrypoints == m6_direct_write_entrypoints, 0 old-semantic normal entrypoints) is CORRECT, but three of its stated REASONS are factually wrong: (a) the legacy-DB reindex branch does NOT publish to M6 via _unit_processor (it does not route through _unit_processor and certify writes to index-v2.db not index-m6.db); (b) the watch path does NOT use reindex_file_impl (it spawns a full index subprocess); (c) the _watch.py docstring is misleading. These reasoning errors do not change the verdict because the bypass code is unreachable in normal mode, but they should be corrected in the denominator so future reviewers are not misled. PASS, conditional on index.db never being created in normal mode — which the code confirms at runner.py:506-510 and _unit_processor.py:601.
